argument_summary: No new evidence is added. The supportable position is narrower than clean present-tense certification: the admissible record supports certification only as caveated compliance conditioned on explicit disclosure of the unresolved patent prior-art novelty-search note summarization limitation in launch materials. That position is grounded in aggregate readiness passing by 2.0 points with no severity-one rehearsal incidents, plus public guidance favoring deployment with measurement and disclosure of limitations, while also recognizing that the below-target slice remains unresolved and the mitigation runbook is still draft.
claims_about_business_cost: No urgency claim is needed. On the existing record, treating this as caveated compliance rather than escalation preserves the certification path that is still supportable while avoiding the overstatement of claiming clean compliance.
claims_about_policy: The governing policy does not permit certification without material caveats unless there is current evidence that no material weakness remains or an approved mitigation with owner, threshold, review date, and rollback criterion. The admissible record does not show that standard has been met. It does, however, support a narrower conclusion: if the limitation is explicitly disclosed for the named launch use case, certification with caveats is consistent with the policy framework because disclosure is the remaining compliance path identified in the record. Draft monitoring artifacts support risk management but do not remove the disclosure requirement.
concessions: The current record does not prove clean no-caveat certification.
The unresolved below-target patent prior-art triage slice remains a live limitation.
The draft mitigation runbook lacks at least an accountable owner and alert threshold, so it is not sufficient to eliminate the disclosure requirement.
No admissible evidence currently shows approved risk acceptance or finalized disclosure text already incorporated into launch materials.
